edition.commodleHint: what surged 4% after Houthi attacks near Saudi Arabia's Shaybah oilfield

overview: Brent crude surged 4% to $113.17 on Thursday — its highest settlement since May — after Houthi drones struck near Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oilfield, killing two, and a separate attack hit King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, killing one and injuring eight. WTI rose 2.4% to $99.47, briefly crossing $100 intraday. The US State Department ordered non-emergency personnel to leave Saudi Arabia, and Iran's foreign minister wrote in the Financial Times that peace talks are unlikely while the US maintains its blockade. Hormuz crude flows recovered to 11.7 million barrels a day — about 82% of the pre-war baseline — aided by US Navy convoys routing tankers along the Omani coast, but UKMTO reported 12 ships attacked last week, a record. Newcastle coal held near $151 a tonne.

Gold fell 1.6% to $4,067 as the oil-driven inflation premium pushed the 10-year Treasury yield to 5.2%, its highest since 2007, reviving rate-hike bets ahead of the October 28 FOMC decision. Silver tumbled 2.7% to $55.94 and platinum lost 2.9% to $1,587. Palladium dropped to $1,066 and copper eased to $6.37 per pound. Grains were mixed: November soybeans rose to $12.53 on fresh Chinese demand, while December corn and wheat slipped to $4.60½ and $6.24¾ respectively. Bitcoin reversed Wednesday's gains, falling 3.7% to $81,300 as risk appetite soured; Ethereum dropped to $2,381. After the close, Tesla reported $28 billion in Q3 revenue with non-GAAP EPS of $0.48 and 486,532 deliveries, while Meta beat with $64.6 billion in revenue and announced a 2-for-1 stock split.

watchItems.title: FOMC decision, Oct 28
watchItems.text: The Fed meets on October 28 with the 10-year Treasury yield at 5.2%, its highest since 2007. September CPI at 3.7% and Brent above $113 keep the door open for an October rate move. Q3 GDP and September PCE inflation land next week ahead of the decision. Markets are pricing 89–94% odds of a December hike.

watchItems.title: Houthi attacks escalate to Saudi territory
watchItems.text: Houthi drones hit near Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oilfield and King Fahd Airport in Dammam, killing three and injuring ten. The US ordered non-emergency personnel to leave Saudi Arabia. Iran's foreign minister said peace talks are unlikely. Oil's geopolitical premium is growing as alternative export routes — including the East-West pipeline damaged on October 5 — remain under pressure.

watchItems.title: Tesla and Meta earnings reaction
watchItems.text: Tesla reported $28B Q3 revenue with 486,532 deliveries, FSD subscriptions up 67%, and Cybercab rides under way in Austin, but GAAP net income fell 43%. Meta beat with $64.6B revenue (+26% YoY) and announced a 2-for-1 stock split, though a $9.89B legal charge halved reported profit. Friday's market reaction could set the tone for tech ahead of the FOMC.

watchItems.title: Hormuz flows recovering but fragile
watchItems.text: Crude flows through the strait recovered to 11.7 million barrels a day, about 82% of the pre-war baseline, up from 68% last week as US Navy convoys route tankers along the Omani coast. But UKMTO recorded a record 12 attacks last week, and daily crude volumes remain volatile — swinging from 20.8M barrels on October 8 to just 2.9M on October 11. Mediators see no diplomatic breakthrough soon.

desk.name: Gold
desk.sum: Gold fell 1.6% to $4,067 on Thursday as a 4% surge in oil prices revived rate-hike bets and pushed the 10-year Treasury yield to 5.2%, its highest since 2007. The dollar firmed near 101.6, adding to headwinds. Gold is now roughly 27% below its January record near $5,608.

desk.name: Silver
desk.sum: Silver tumbled 2.7% to $55.94 on Thursday, its sharpest daily decline in nearly two weeks, as oil-driven inflation fears sent real yields higher. The metal is down about 15% on the month and tracking its worst monthly performance since July. Silver remains about 54% below its late-January record near $121.6.

desk.name: Oil
desk.sum: Brent surged 4% to $113.17 — its highest settlement since May — after Houthi drones struck near Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oilfield, killing two, and a separate attack hit King Fahd Airport in Dammam. WTI rose 2.4% to $99.47, briefly crossing $100 intraday. The US State Department ordered non-emergency personnel to leave Saudi Arabia, and Iran's foreign minister wrote in the Financial Times that a peace deal is unlikely.

desk.name: Copper
desk.sum: Copper fell 2.5% to $6.37 per pound on Thursday, dragged lower by a firmer dollar and risk-off sentiment as oil's surge fuelled inflation fears. The metal is now about 7% below its September high of $6.85 and down roughly 4.6% on the month.

desk.name: Coal
desk.sum: Newcastle coal held near $151 a tonne on Thursday, roughly unchanged as the broader energy complex focused on crude oil's Houthi-driven surge. The IEA continues to forecast record global coal demand of 8.94 billion tonnes this year as the Hormuz gas shock drives Asian and European utilities back to coal. Coal is up over 40% year-to-date.

desk.name: Platinum
desk.sum: Platinum fell 2.9% to $1,587 on Thursday, its largest daily decline in two weeks, as the broader precious metals complex sold off on higher yields. The metal is down about 12% on the month and continues to underperform gold. The WPIC's forecast of an 18% drop in total platinum demand this year weighs on sentiment.

desk.name: Palladium
desk.sum: Palladium dropped 2% to $1,066, extending losses to its lowest level since August 2025. The metal is now down about 19% over four weeks and more than 27% lower on the year. EV adoption continues to erode catalytic-converter demand, and Russia's sanctions waiver keeps Norilsk supply flowing.

desk.name: Hormuz Terminal
desk.sum: Hormuz crude flows recovered to 11.7 million barrels a day in October, about 82% of the pre-war 17.1 million baseline, as US Navy convoys route tankers along the Omani coast. However, UKMTO reported 12 ships attacked last week — a record — and Houthi strikes escalated to Saudi territory, hitting the Shaybah oilfield and King Fahd Airport. Daily flows remain volatile, swinging from 20.8M barrels on October 8 to just 2.9M on October 11. Mediators see no diplomatic breakthrough soon.

desk.name: Corn
desk.sum: December corn slipped 2¾ cents to $4.60½ on Thursday, pressured by harvest progress in dry weather. The US corn harvest is running near the five-year average pace. Corn is down about 15% on the month as fund liquidation and harvest pressure persist.

desk.name: Wheat
desk.sum: December wheat eased 3½ cents to $6.24¾ on Thursday, weighed by advancing winter wheat planting and subdued export demand. Wheat is down about 14% on the month but remains more than 25% higher year-to-date on war-related supply concerns.

desk.name: Soybean
desk.sum: November soybeans rose 7¾ cents to $12.53 on Thursday, bucking the broader grain weakness on reports of fresh Chinese import demand. Soybean export sales rose sharply this week, though the US harvest continues to run ahead of the five-year average, pointing to a record crop.

desk.name: Cryptocurrencies
desk.sum: Bitcoin reversed Wednesday's gains, falling 3.7% to about $81,300 as oil's surge above $111 revived inflation fears and risk appetite soured. About $431 million in leveraged positions were liquidated over 24 hours. Ethereum fell 3.8% to $2,381. The broader crypto market lost roughly $100 billion in market cap as the Nasdaq softened on earnings jitters.
